result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: In parseAmount, the symbol-stripping regex `/[\s€$£¥]/g` only removes whitespace and a hardcoded set of currency symbols (€$£¥); it does not include ₹ (rupee) or alphabetic prefixes like 'CHF '. Broaden the stripping logic (e.g. strip any leading non-digit/sign currency symbol or known currency code prefix) so amounts like '₹1,250.00' and 'CHF 1'200.00' parse correctly.
result.evidence: parseAmount in src/util/money.ts does `raw.replace(/[\s€$£¥]/g, "")` before validating with `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`; since ₹ and letters like CHF are not stripped, the regex test fails and the function returns null, producing 'The amount is not a number' (src/i18n/en.json).

not_searched: How CSV import invokes parseAmount and whether currency codes are passed in separately
Whether CHF uses ' (apostrophe) as thousands separator elsewhere in the codebase

text: The regex `[\s€$£¥]` strips only euro, dollar, pound, yen symbols—not ₹ (rupee) or multi-char prefixes like "CHF ". This confirms the bug.

input.title: Broaden currency symbol stripping in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

In parseAmount, the symbol-stripping regex only removes whitespace and a hardcoded set of currency symbols (€$£¥), missing ₹ and alphabetic prefixes like "CHF ". Broaden the stripping logic (e.g. strip any leading non-digit/sign currency symbol or known currency code prefix) so amounts like "₹1,250.00" and "CHF 1'200.00" parse correctly instead of failing validation.
